misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program DamagePokemon
kamus
  attackerTipe, defenderTipe : string
  attackerLevel, defenderLevel : integer
  efektivitas : real
  selisihLevel, levelBonus, tempDiff, damage : integer
algoritma
  input(attackerTipe, attackerLevel)
  input(defenderTipe, defenderLevel)
  if attackerTipe == defenderTipe then
    efektivitas <- 1
  else if attackerTipe == "fire" and defenderTipe == "grass" then
    efektivitas <- 2
  else if attackerTipe == "grass" and defenderTipe == "water" then
    efektivitas <- 2
  else if attackerTipe == "water" and defenderTipe == "fire" then
    efektivitas <- 2
  else
    efektivitas <- 0.5
  endif
  selisihLevel <- attackerLevel - defenderLevel
  levelBonus <- 0
  tempDiff <- selisihLevel
  if tempDiff > 0 then
    levelBonus <- levelBonus + 1
    tempDiff <- tempDiff - 1
  endif
  damage <- bulat(((2 * attackerLevel) / 5 + 2) * (attackerLevel / defenderLevel) * efektivitas * levelBonus / 10)
  if damage < 1 then
    damage <- 1
  endif
  output(damage)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes the if-statement will execute repeatedly like a while loop. They want to calculate a level_bonus based on the level difference, so they set up an if-statement that decrements temp_diff and increments level_bonus, expecting it to loop until temp_diff reaches 0. In reality, the if-block only executes once, so level_bonus will only be 1 (instead of the full level_diff value they expect). This causes incorrect damage calculations. The student genuinely believes this approach will accumulate the proper level_bonus by "looping" through the if-statement.
